messages:
marta: Quick sync — we've been running the policy bakeoffs. High-level question: do we keep score normalization in adapters or central resolver? Thoughts?

kai: I lean central resolver. Have adapters emit raw signals (latency, cost, region_score) and keep normalization logic in one place. Easier to audit and change. :+1:

devon: Bakeoff data shows adapter-side normalization buys a few percentage points on tail latency in some runtimes (esp older CPUs). But it added complexity for ops and version drift.

rachana: If adapters normalize differently we risk non-composable scores across runtimes/regions. Resolver needs a stable scale to compare candidates. Also affects caching keys (normalized score in cache).

sasha: Middle ground: adapters emit typed signals + an optional confidence metric, resolver applies tenant/policy-specific normalization functions. Adapter contract becomes minimal: {signal: value, confidence: 0-1}.

marta: Example raw payload we currently log:
```json
{"lat_ms": 32, "cost_cents": 0.0034, "region": "us-west-2", "tail_p95": 85}
```
If we require adapters to return a single normalized score, they'd need to implement the same formula as resolver — that duplicates logic and creates drift.

kai: Also: telemetry requirement — we must trace raw signals -> normalized score -> final decision for audits + regressions. That favors central normalization and clear tracepoints in the resolver path.

devon: Perf note: doing normalization in the resolver adds CPU on the hot path. Bakeoff numbers: ~1-2% median increase, ~8% for tiny requests that are CPU-bound. But we can memoize normalization per model/tenant/routing-window.

rachana: Tie-breaking needs to be explicit. Suggest deterministic order: prefer same region, then lower cost, then replica hash. No randomness. Documented in DSL.

sasha: We should support adapter-level overrides for special runtimes (on-prem, fixed pricing). Proposal: adapter can set `pre_normalized: true` + `schema_version`. Resolver will accept pre-normalized scores only when schema matches and adapter declares the formula.

marta: I'm leaning toward central normalization + optional adapter pre-normalized flag with required schema and formula doc. That gives us control and escape hatches.

kai: We should add a small DSL extension for this: `normalization: builtin|custom` and `tie_break: [region, cost, replica_hash]`. Sketch:
```yaml
policies:
  - id: latency_first
    objective: latency
    normalization: builtin
    tie_break: [region, cost]
```

devon: Action items: (1) update adapter spec to emit typed signals + optional pre_normalized flag; (2) implement memoized normalizer in resolver; (3) add telemetry tracepoints for raw->normalized->decision; (4) migration plan for existing adapters.

rachana: I'll own (1) and the spec doc. Will include examples + backwards compatibility notes.

sasha: I'll take (2) (resolver change) and coordinate perf tests with eng-runtime.

devon: I'll add tracepoints and a small evaluation harness to validate decisions (3).

marta: I'll draft the migration plan and rollout schedule (4). Timeline suggestion: spec + tests in 2 weeks, resolver work ~3 weeks, staged rollout by tenant groups.

policy-bot: New RFC draft created: rfc/2026-routing-normalization-proposal.md (https://redwood.internal/rfc/2026) :robot_face:

sasha: One more ask — add eval cases that simulate cross-region failure + cost spikes. We must ensure normalization doesn't favor cheap-but-slow under those patterns.

kai: Agreed. Also run A/B over a small tenant cohort to compare decision distributions before full rollout.

marta: Perfect. Thanks all. :rocket:
